manifest.prompt: make a compact, minimal, modern shopping component.
manifest.built: lite: discover (1 page, 0 video, 0 image) → scrape found page → exclusion, 3 specialists (anatomy, style, interaction) → synthesis → 2 verify; no moodboard (no images found), no gap round
how_to_read: 1. Read the head first: the first 28 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=28, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' shop-component.metadump.json).
2. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' shop-component.metadump.json
3. Also pull the anti-keywords and review prompts (checks) for your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' shop-component.metadump.json
4. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' shop-component.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
5. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' shop-component.metadump.json returns whole entries.

essence.one_sentence: A compact, minimal, modern shopping component: one product, a short set of parts, one accent for the single cart action, and no decoration beyond what buying needs.

poles: visible focus, named controls and disabled states

routing.job: always first: the defining tier-1 entries
routing.when: pull first for any job: the most relevant entries (relevance, not rules)
before picking type, color or spacing

routing.job: check an output against the dump

ak-gradient-surface.instead: one flat solid surface color, separated from the page by a 1px hairline border or by spacing alone

ak-heavy-shadow.instead: no shadow, or one very soft low-elevation shadow used only to lift the card; the border carries the edge

ak-glass-blur.instead: an opaque solid surface; no translucency, no backdrop blur

ak-saturated-accents.instead: neutral surfaces and text with one accent color, used only on the add-to-cart control and the sale price

ak-icon-overload.instead: text labels for fields and actions; at most one icon, a cart glyph beside the add-to-cart label if any

ak-emoji-badge.instead: a plain text pill in the neutral palette, for example Sale or New, with no emoji

ak-oversized-card.instead: a card sized to its content, with padding and gaps drawn from one small spacing scale (for example 8, 12, 16 px)

ak-stock-hero.instead: the product image at the card's own aspect ratio, or a neutral placeholder block if no image is supplied

ak-filler-copy.instead: the real short product name and price; a description only when the product data supplies one

ak-carousel-gallery.instead: a single product image; add more images only when the user asks for them

ak-bouncy-motion.instead: a short ease-out transition on the add-to-cart state change, with no overshoot and no bounce

ak-heavy-type.instead: one sans-serif family in two or three weights (regular, medium, semibold) on a small type scale

ak-minimal-drops-access.instead: keep a visible focus ring, real button text, and readable text contrast; minimal limits decoration, not accessibility

k-compact.text: The component is visibly compact: few parts, tight spacing, no decorative extras.

test.spec: count the parts; anything beyond image, name, price and one add-to-cart action needs a reason

k-modern.text: The look is contemporary: flat surfaces, restrained type, no skeuomorphic or heavy effects.

test.spec: no gradient surface, no heavy drop shadow, no glass blur

k-one-cart-action.text: Exactly one add-to-cart action per card.

test.spec: one primary cart control in the card
disabled or hidden when the variant is unavailable

k-no-emoji-badges.text: No emoji badges or icon overload.

test.spec: no emoji characters in the component markup or labels

k-no-bounce.text: Motion is brief and not bouncy.

test.spec: feedback durations stay short, no overshoot

k-focus-visible.text: Keyboard focus is visible on every control.

test.spec: focus ring visible on the add-to-cart button when tabbed to

k-named-cart-button.text: The add-to-cart button has an accessible name that includes the product name.

q-framework.text: Which framework or platform (React, Vue, plain HTML, SwiftUI)?
q-framework.default: framework-agnostic HTML, CSS and a small amount of JavaScript

q-product.text: What product is sold, and which fields does the component show?
q-product.default: a generic single product: image, name, price, quantity, add-to-cart

q-scope.text: Is the component a product card, a product detail panel, or a cart line?
q-scope.default: a product card with an add-to-cart control

q-addtocart-states.text: The ProductCard page does not describe add-to-cart states (idle, pressed, adding, added, disabled). It only says the UI should be gated on availableForSale.
q-addtocart-states.default: idle, pressed, adding, added, disabled; disabled whenever availableForSale is false

q-price-display.text: The page does not state currency symbol, decimal places, or how sale and strike-through prices render.
q-price-display.default: currency symbol and two decimals from the amount string; compareAtPrice struck through before the current price when non-null

q-surface-cues.text: The page does not state surface, border or shadow. Its preview image was linked but not fetched, so no visual cues were read.
q-surface-cues.default: take surface, border and shadow values from the style section's options, not from this page

q-compact-fields.text: The page does not list which fields the compact variant shows.
q-compact-fields.default: product image, title and price only

q-quantity-default.text: Does the minimal build include a quantity stepper? The q-product default lists quantity, but the prompt asks for minimal.
q-quantity-default.default: no: add-to-cart adds one unit; the stepper stays an option

q-undefined-availability.text: What does the add-to-cart control do when availableForSale is undefined?
q-undefined-availability.default: leave it enabled; disable it only when the flag is false

q-card-width.text: What width should the compact card have?
q-card-width.default: 200 to 320 px, fluid within its grid cell

q-style-radius.text: Which corner radius: square (4 px), soft (8 px) or round (12 px)?
q-style-radius.default: 8 px, one value shared by the card and the add-to-cart control

q-style-accent.text: Which single accent color should mark add-to-cart and the sale price?

q-style-dark.text: Light only, or also a dark variant?
q-style-dark.default: light only; dark as an option in opt-dark-mode

q-style-type.text: System UI font stack, or a named web font?

q-no-video.text: No video of an add-to-cart control was found, so press and confirmation durations are not measured.

q-hold-duration.text: The 1.2 to 2 s return time comes from discovery notes that cite web examples; no fetched page confirms it.
q-hold-duration.default: 1500 ms, inside the 1200 to 2000 ms option range

q-reduced-motion-source.text: Reduced-motion handling and the focus ring contrast are general practice, not sourced from a fetched page.
q-reduced-motion-source.default: remove movement and keep the label change; 2 px ring at 3:1 contrast

q-live-region.text: No source decides whether the confirmation uses a live region or moves focus to a status line.
q-live-region.default: polite live region; focus stays on the button

brief._about: Literal requirements from the prompt. Nothing added here.

p-shopping-component.text: The deliverable is a shopping component: a UI component for buying a product.

p-compact.text: The component is compact: small footprint, few elements, tight spacing.

p-minimal.text: The component is minimal: only the elements needed to shop, no decorative extras.

p-modern.text: The component looks and behaves like current (contemporary) interface design.

product_card_api._about: Facts stated by the ProductCard page of the Shop Minis React SDK. These are this SDK's props and types; read them as its contract, not as general web conventions.

sc-variants.text: ProductCard has three variants set by the variant prop: default (product grids where details matter), priceOverlay (visual-first feeds) and compact (limited space).
never_implies: that the compact variant hides specific fields; the page does not list them

sc-compact-example.text: The page describes the compact variant as a product card with minimal information and shows it rendered with only product and variant="compact" passed.

sc-productlink.text: For some list views where space is limited, the page suggests ProductLink may work better than ProductCard.

sc-availability-gate.text: A variant's availableForSale flag says whether it can be purchased. When false, add-to-cart and buy calls through the SDK fail, so the UI should be gated on the flag. The field may be undefined when the source has no stock state.

sc-money.text: Prices arrive as a Money object: amount is a decimal string (the example uses '702.95') and currencyCode is an ISO 4217 code (the example uses 'USD'). The page does not state rounding, symbol placement or grouping.

sc-compare-at-price.text: compareAtPrice is a Money value or null on both the product and each variant. The page types the field but does not say how a compare-at price is displayed.

sc-favorite.text: The card has a favorite control: isFavorited on the product gives its state, onFavoriteToggled(isFavorited) fires on toggle, and favoriteButtonDisabled disables the button.

sc-touchable.text: touchable controls whether the card can be clicked or tapped to navigate to product details. onProductClick fires when the product is clicked.

sc-badge.text: An optional badgeText string appears in a badge on the card. badgeVariant is 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'destructive' | 'outline' | 'none'.

sc-reviews.text: reviewAnalytics (averageRating and reviewCount, both optional) feeds the review stars. reviewsDisabled turns the stars off.

sc-selected-variant.text: selectedProductVariant is an optional ProductVariant that shows variant-specific data. Products carry options (for example Color, Size) and each variant lists selectedOptions as name and value pairs.

sc-children.text: children takes a custom layout. The page says ProductCard exposes composable subcomponents for custom layouts.

anatomy._about: Parts, states and optional pieces of a compact shopping component. The minimal part set and the states are inferred from the prompt; the ProductCard facts (sc-*) are the Shop Minis SDK contract and are read as its contract, not as general web convention.

an-parts-minimal.text: The minimum set is four parts: product image, product name, price, and one add-to-cart control. Nothing else is needed to shop. A component without all four is not a complete shopping component.
never_implies: that a quantity stepper, badge, rating or variant selector is forbidden
that the parts must stack in a fixed order beyond the image coming first

an-compact-footprint.text: Compact means one product, a small image, a short text block and one control, all in a single column with tight spacing. The component never grows into a detail panel, a tab set or a multi-step flow.
never_implies: that small type or small touch targets are acceptable

an-part-image.text: The product image is the top part of the card at a fixed aspect ratio, so cards line up in a grid. It is the only part that is not text or a control.
never_implies: a specific aspect ratio (see the options area)

an-part-name.text: The product name sits directly under the image in the card's strongest text style. It is one line by default and truncates with an ellipsis beyond that.
never_implies: a specific font family or size

an-part-price.text: The current price sits under the name on its own line. It is formatted from the Money object: the amount string (for example '702.95') with the decimal places of its currencyCode, and the currency shown as a symbol or code.
never_implies: that every shop prices in USD

an-part-add-to-cart.text: The add-to-cart control is the last part of the card and the only action on it. It carries the card's single primary emphasis and is sized to its label or fills the card width.
never_implies: a specific label text, which belongs to the copy layer
that a buy-now button also appears

inv-single-cart-action.invariant: exactly one add-to-cart control per card, and it is the only control that changes cart state
inv-single-cart-action.variable: its label text, width, icon and placement inside the bottom row
inv-single-cart-action.text: A card never shows two cart actions. Any extra control must not change cart state.

inv-availability-gate.invariant: add-to-cart is disabled whenever the variant's availableForSale is false
inv-availability-gate.variable: how the disabled state looks (color, label, icon)
inv-availability-gate.text: Gate the control on availableForSale. The SDK page says the field may be undefined when the source has no stock state, so undefined is not treated as false; see q-undefined-availability.

b-compact-minimal.text: 'compact' and 'minimal' describe the footprint and the number of parts only. They do not describe type size, contrast or target size.
never_implies: small type or touch targets below readable size

then: one badge on a corner of the image, styled by badgeVariant (primary, secondary, destructive, outline or none)
no badge when badgeText is absent
g-optional-badge.text: The badge is optional and appears only when there is badge text to show.

when.compareAtPrice: non-null and greater than the current amount

then: the compare-at price struck through, placed before the current price
g-compare-price.text: A sale shows the original price struck through next to the current price. Without a higher compare-at value, the price line shows the current price alone.

an-state-idle.text: Idle is the default: enabled, at rest, with no spinner and no check mark.

an-state-pressed.text: Pressed gives immediate feedback while the pointer or finger is down. It is a visual change only; no request is sent until release.

an-state-adding.text: Adding means a cart request is in flight. The control is disabled against repeat taps, shows a progress indicator, and keeps its width so the layout does not shift.

an-state-added.text: Added means the request succeeded. The control briefly confirms (a check mark or a changed label), then returns to idle so the user can add again.

an-state-disabled.text: Disabled applies when availableForSale is false or a request is blocked. The control is not clickable, keeps its size, and is exposed to assistive tech as disabled.

p-price-decimals.text: Show the decimal places that the currency's minor unit defines: two for USD. Take the count from the currency, not from the length of the amount string.

opt-part-quantity.text: A quantity stepper (minus, count, plus, default 1) beside the add-to-cart control. The minimal set leaves it out, so add-to-cart adds one unit. Add it when a product sells in several units per order.

p-card-width.text: Width of one compact card in a grid cell, 200 to 320 px. 280 px is a starting point for a desktop grid, not a measured value.

style._about: Visual style for a compact, minimal, modern shopping component. No reference image was supplied and the scraped page gives no visual values, so nothing here is sampled or observed. Values marked inferred follow from the prompt words compact, minimal and modern. Numbers and colors in the options group are proposals, not requirements.

st-one-accent.text: The component uses one accent color, and only on the add-to-cart control and the sale price. Everything else is neutral.

st-color-count.text: At most five colors: surface, ink, muted ink, hairline and one accent. No other hues.

st-role-surface.text: One flat solid color for the card and its controls. Not a gradient and not translucent.

st-role-ink.text: Primary text color for the product name and the regular price. A muted ink, a lighter neutral, is used for secondary text such as variant or unit labels.

st-role-hairline.text: A 1px neutral line that draws the card edge and separates parts when spacing alone is not enough. No double borders.

st-role-accent.text: The single accent. It fills or outlines only the add-to-cart control and marks the sale price. Its exact value is an option, see opt-palette.

st-edge-rule.text: The card edge is a 1px hairline border on a flat surface. No shadow by default. A shadow, if used, is the single soft one in opt-shadow.

st-spacing-unit.text: Spacing is built on a 4 px base unit. Every padding, gap and margin is a multiple of it.

st-spacing-steps.text: Common gaps are 8, 12 and 16 px: 8 between tight elements such as name and price, 12 between rows, 16 for card padding. Compact means these steps, not larger ones.

st-type-sizes.text: Three sizes at most: label 12 px, body and product name 14 to 16 px, price 16 to 18 px. Larger display sizes do not belong in a compact component.

st-type-weights.text: Two weights: regular 400 for labels and secondary text, semibold 600 for the product name and price. No 700 and no decorative weights.

opt-radius.text: Corner radius: 8 px as the default. 4 px gives a squarer, more editorial look; 12 px gives a softer one. Use one value for the card and the add-to-cart control alike.

opt-palette.text: Example values, not sourced from any reference: surface #FFFFFF, ink #111827, muted ink #6B7280, hairline #E5E7EB, accent #2563EB. Any neutral set with the same five roles works.

opt-type-family.text: Default: the system UI font stack (system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif). A named web font is the alternative when a brand requires one.

opt-shadow.text: Optional: one very soft shadow, for example a 1px offset with a 2px blur at low opacity, used only to lift the card. The default is no shadow.

opt-dark-mode.text: Light first. A dark variant swaps surface and ink values, keeps the same five roles and the single accent, and keeps the hairline visible. Use it only if the user asks for dark mode.

interaction._about: Motion, states and keyboard behavior for the add-to-cart control. No video of this control was found and no timeline was measured, so no duration in this section is measured. Timing values sit in the options group and are options, not requirements. The one sourced fact is the availableForSale gate (sc-availability-gate). The four feedback states come from the discovery notes, not from a fetched page.

ix-addtocart-states.text: The add-to-cart control moves through idle, pressed, adding, added and disabled. Idle is the resting label. Pressed is pointer or key down. Adding is the request in flight. Added confirms the item went into the cart. Disabled applies when the variant is not purchasable. Discovery notes name four feedback states, idle, loading, success and error; loading is adding, success is added, and error is covered by ix-error-state.

ix-error-state.text: If the add request fails, the control returns to idle and a short inline message sits beside it, for example 'Could not add. Try again.' Discovery notes list error as a feedback state; no fetched source says how it looks.

ix-no-layout-shift.text: The add-to-cart control keeps the same width and height in every state. The label changes inside a fixed box, so the card does not reflow during adding or added.

ix-add-confirmation.text: On success the label changes to Added, with an optional check glyph, and the control stays in place for a short hold before it returns to idle. The return is a state change, not a dismissal. The added state is also announced through a polite live region reading 'Added [product name] to cart'. Focus does not move.

ix-disabled-gate.text: When availableForSale is false, the add-to-cart control is disabled and a visible reason such as 'Sold out' sits beside it, since a disabled button alone gives no reason. When the field is undefined the source has no stock state, so do not disable on undefined alone.

ix-bind-minimal-motion.text: 'minimal' binds to the count of moving parts, not to the absence of feedback: one property changes per state change, and the state stays visible.

ix-reduced-motion.invariant: every state change is still conveyed by its label or text
ix-reduced-motion.variable: transition duration, easing and any movement
ix-reduced-motion.text: When the user asks for reduced motion, remove movement and keep the state change. The label carries the state; any motion left is an opacity change with no transform. The standard media query is prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. This is general web practice, not a fetched source.

ix-focus-visible.invariant: a keyboard focus indicator is visible on the add-to-cart control, the favorite toggle and the card link wherever they can take focus
never_implies: that minimal removes the focus ring
ix-focus-visible.text: Keyboard focus shows a visible ring on every focusable control in the card, and no state removes it. Minimal limits decoration around the ring; it does not limit the ring. The options group gives a ring spec.

ix-focus-order.text: Tab order follows visual order inside a card: product link or title (when the card is touchable), then the favorite toggle, then add-to-cart. Enter and Space activate the focused button through native button behavior. The decorative product image is not in the tab order.

ix-addtocart-name.text: The visible label is 'Add to cart' and it starts the accessible name. Where several cards share a page, add the product name in visually hidden text after the label, so the name reads 'Add to cart' followed by the product name. Do not replace the visible label with an aria-label that drops its words.

ix-opt-press-duration.text: Press feedback on pointer or key down: about 100 ms, ease-out, no overshoot. Pick one treatment: a one-step color darken or a scale to 0.98. Not both.

ix-opt-state-change.text: Label change between idle, adding and added: about 150 ms, ease-out, no overshoot, the same curve for every state change.

ix-opt-added-hold.text: Time the Added label stays before the control returns to Add to cart. Discovery notes cite about 1.2 to 2 s from web examples; no fetched page confirms it.

ix-opt-focus-ring.text: Focus ring 2 px solid with a 2 px offset, colored for at least 3:1 contrast against the card surface. Illustrative; the contrast rule is general accessibility practice.

ix-opt-reduced-motion.text: Reduced motion treatment: either an instant state change, or an opacity-only fade of about 100 ms. Pick one; both keep the label change.

w-productcard.title: ProductCard (Shop Minis React SDK docs)
w-productcard.quote: Optimized for grid layouts with three variants: default, priceOverlay, and compact.
